title: Module 01 — Introduction to Deep Learning and TensorFlow

audio.note: Scene durations below are frame-aligned (30fps) to the natural pauses in this VO. Total = 3851 frames = 128.36s.

items: What deep learning actually is
Why it dominated ML over the last decade
Three anchors: representations, chain rule, SGD
A deep net is a stack of differentiable functions
Power comes from composition, not a single clever layer
Training = minimize a scalar loss by gradient descent
Gradients flow backward through the chain rule
ImageNet 2012 — AlexNet halved top-5 error
GPU compute unlocked billion-parameter training
ReLU, batch norm, residual links stabilized depth
Open source frameworks made it accessible

props.title: TensorFlow, Keras, and eager execution
props.subtitle: One stack, three levels of abstraction

items: tf.Tensor — dense multi-dimensional arrays on CPU/GPU
tf.function — traces Python into a compiled graph
Keras — the high-level model API most courses teach
GradientTape — manual differentiation for custom loops

props.title: Gradient descent in 30 seconds
props.subtitle: The engine behind every training run

items: Pick a loss — measures how wrong the model is
Compute ∂loss/∂parameters — the gradient
Step parameters against the gradient: θ ← θ − η·∇loss
Repeat on mini-batches until loss plateaus
Everything else is variance reduction on this core loop
Fundamentals → CNNs → Advanced Training
Segmentation → Detection → GANs
NLP → Time Series → Production Deployment
Every module has theory, labs, and a quiz
Progress tracked locally — your data never leaves the device
